latest.title: MIT’s SwarmWorld agent society result holds up on consumer GPUs - The Next Web
latest.summary: In August, researchers at MIT dropped a society of AI agents into a shared world with no instructions. They showed it could invent, build and maintain technology better than the same number of agents ...
highlights: In August, researchers at MIT dropped a society of AI agents into a shared world with no instructions. They showed it could invent, build and maintain technology better than the same number of agents working alone. The study ran on a hosted frontier model. A research team working with Apex Fusion has now reproduced the central experiment on four RTX 3090 gaming GPUs. Apex Fusion is a Swiss foundation building infrastructure for AI agents. The MIT team released its code, prompts and complete traces, which is what made an outside replication possible. The replication, led by Časlav Nedeljković of HAL8, set out to test whether SwarmWorld’s result depended on a frontier model. The replication itself ran directly on the team’s own GPUs. The team also registered its model server as a supplier on the Vector marketplace, an OpenAI-compatible gateway that meters each request and settles usage on-chain in AP3X, the network’s utility token.

latest.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says AI will create more programmers, not replace them - Ynetnews
latest.summary: ## At GTC Berlin 2026, Nvidia unveils safeguards against rogue AI agents powered by Israeli-developed chips, a humanoid robot and advances in self-driving cars and cancer research, as Huang argues AI ...
highlights: ## At GTC Berlin 2026, Nvidia unveils safeguards against rogue AI agents powered by Israeli-developed chips, a humanoid robot and advances in self-driving cars and cancer research, as Huang argues AI will expand opportunities for software developers. Artificial intelligence will not eliminate programmers but will instead increase their numbers, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said Wednesday at the company's GTC Berlin 2026 conference, where the technology giant unveiled new safeguards for autonomous AI agents, humanoid robots and advances in self-driving vehicles and cancer treatment. "More people will write programs using the new tools, and every company will become an AI company." He also highlighted the dramatic growth in AI computing power, saying that the processing capabilities of the company's AI chips had increased 1,000-fold since their introduction. The company has become central to the development and operation of increasingly powerful AI systems, positioning it to shape not only how the technology advances but also how it is controlled.

latest.title: Nvidia OpenShell gets a hardware stack for Anthropic and OpenAI agents - The Next Web
latest.summary: Nvidia has released a design for running AI agents inside fixed limits, from enterprise infrastructure to edge machines. Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, Google Cloud and AWS are among the companie...
highlights: Nvidia has released a design for running AI agents inside fixed limits, from enterprise infrastructure to edge machines. Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta, Microsoft, Google Cloud and AWS are among the companies working with it, Nvidia said. The design builds on OpenShell, Nvidia’s open source runtime software, which sets a boundary around what an agent can do. OpenShell is also part of the agent safety platform Nvidia launched in September. The software that drives the agents and their tools runs on Vera CPUs. BlueField-4 data processing units run Nvidia Sentry, software that watches agent behaviour from outside the main system. If an agent tries to move outside its software boundary, Sentry quarantines and stops it in milliseconds, Nvidia said. Agents from Anthropic, Cohere, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Perplexity, Reflection and SpaceX Super Intelligence can run on OpenShell infrastructure, Nvidia said. > “With the OpenShell Reference Architecture, agents can think on Rubin, act on Vera and be governed on BlueField,” Huang said.

latest.summary: # Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet. The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands. Ant...
highlights: # Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet. The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands. Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, introduced an A.I. agent on Wednesday that acts as a personal digital assistant. Called Claude Duet, the tool is in an early test phase but joins a fast-growing field of A.I. assistants that take actions and perform tasks on their own. It will compete with OpenAI’s dots, which debuted last month; Meta’s Muse; Google’s Gemini Spark; and agents from the start-up Instinct, which raised $1 billion in its latest funding round. Unlike OpenAI and Meta, which have pitched their agents as assistants for everyday tasks like booking reservations, Anthropic said Claude Duet was built for work and was less capable at personal errands. Claude Duet is Anthropic’s most direct attempt to move its chatbot from answering questions to running parts of people’s working lives.

highlights: South Korea's AI trade roared back Wednesday, as stocks staged a dramatic rebound from Tuesday's rout and a disastrous AI IPO reversed course. The benchmark Kospi index surged as much as 5%, triggering a temporary curb on program buying as investors piled back into heavyweight chipmakers. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix jumped as much as 8% and 9%, respectively, helping reverse Tuesday's market rout. The Kospi more than doubled in the first half of the year, powered by an AI-driven memory-chip boom. The latest whiplash was particularly dramatic for Elice, an AI cloud and data center operator listed on the Kosdaq. The reversal was especially striking given the frenzy surrounding Elice's IPO, which drew institutional and retail demand by about 400 times. Elice, which started as an education technology company before expanding into AI infrastructure, reported a 200% year-over-year jump in first-half revenue to 34.4 billion won, or $26 million and an operating profit of 10.3 billion won, according to its IPO prospectus.

highlights: A quarter of Meta Muse's 10 million users are shopping online via the AI agent with an average spend of $200 per purchase, according to Mark Zuckerberg. We’re about to be immersed in the busiest shopping season of the year, and if Mark Zuckerberg has his way, people will completely hand over the responsibility of buying stuff to their own personal AI agent. During the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, Zuckerberg said that over a quarter of Meta Muse‘s engaged users — now totaling more than 10 million — were using the AI agent for shopping, with an “average purchase size of over $200.”. Now that the AI agent has achieved what Zuckerberg referred to as a “product-market fit,” the name of the game for Muse in the long term is that we may be living in a reality where you have your own personal AI agent communicating with a business’s AI agent to complete transactions without you ever needing to speak with someone directly.

week.title: Nvidia and its sidekick Nokia claim European enthusiasm for AI-RAN - Telecoms
week.summary: # Nvidia and its sidekick Nokia claim European enthusiasm for AI-RAN. US chip giant Nvidia is using its big European conference to announce a bunch of operator initiatives that make use of its product...
highlights: # Nvidia and its sidekick Nokia claim European enthusiasm for AI-RAN. US chip giant Nvidia is using its big European conference to announce a bunch of operator initiatives that make use of its products. Among the flood of press releases emanating from Nvidia’s GTC (GPU Technology Conference) in Berlin was one declaring “Nvidia, Nokia and leading telecom operators turn networks into distributed intelligence platforms”. In support of that claim, a bunch of European operators issued their own releases extolling the virtues of injecting GPUs into networks. The Telecoms.com inbox was bombarded by emails from BT, DT, Orange, TIM, and Elisa, all stressing their enthusiasm for AI-RAN and patting Nokia on the head for its dutiful assistance with the matter. “Leading global operators are turning their land, power and connectivity into a distributed AI infrastructure — bringing intelligence closer to the industries, people and robots that use it. “Nvidia and Nokia are combining CUDA accelerated computing and AI with Nokia’s network software and expertise to improve radio performance and deploy trusted AI agents.
